newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 11.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Last night's Parliament debate on social dialogue between government, unions and employers on changes to the job market was a substantial discussion between government and opposition on major economc, social and political problems. Addresses by Prime Minister Costas Simitis and main opposition leader Costas Karamanlis illustrated the degree of agreement on the goals of the two parties.

--The announcement of a joint Greek-Russian initiative yesterday from Thessaloniki, where Balkan foreign ministers met on regional issues, has brought Greece's leading role to the fore and reactivated Moscow's importance in the region. The foreign ministry officials drafted specific initiatives to bolster economic cooperation and the Greek island of Crete will host a summit of southeast European leaders at the end of the year.

--A new nationwide poll has shown a renaissance in support for conservative opposition party New Democracy following the changing of the guard and the advent of Costas Karamanlis to the presidency. Support for ND increased to 21.0 percent - from 9.6 percent in December 1996 -just 4.6 percent behind ruling party PASOK, while Karamanlis beat out Prime Minister Costas Simitis in the popularity stakes by a head, 44.8 percent to 41.4. Left Coalition leader Nikos Constantopoulos remains most popular however with 52.0 percent.
--Clergy and laymen protesting the Parliament's ratification of the Schengen treaty conducted an all-night vigil outside the building last night.
--The Schengen treaty may have yet to be formally ratified but information indicates that the Greek authorities have been collating information on individuals since last September.
--Karamanlis cracks the whip in Parliament, accusing Simitis of hypocrisy and saying that those who led the country to catastrophe in the 80s were simply wearing a new cap.

--Residents on the holiday isle of Corfu fear they are being surrounded by armed seaborne Albanian pirates ferrying arms and drugs to the island, after the coast guard found a boat loaded with guns and 300kgs of hashish.

--Simitis's high popularity rating is a success for the nine-month-old administration which says it is not governing with an eye on the political cost. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
